evidence.node_done_when: The defect is first reproduced and the reproduction pasted into the manifest: at the current head, tests/test_crew.py::test_double_dispatch_refuses_a_member_with_a_non_terminal_run passes only because pid 4242 is occupied by another user's process, so reckon.crew.node.member_in_flight_verdict reports it alive - os.kill(4242, 0) raises PermissionError, which the liveness helper treats as alive, while ps -p 4242 shows nothing. Demonstrate the dependence by calling member_in_flight_verdict on a pointer whose pid is one that provably does not exist (allocate it by reading /proc/sys/kernel/pid_max or by forking and reaping, and assert os.kill raises ProcessLookupError) and showing the verdict flips to blocks False. Then repair every member-guard test that supplies a literal pid so its outcome no longer depends on the host: the tests must control liveness explicitly rather than hope a number is free or taken, by injecting or monkeypatching the liveness helper, or by using a pid the test itself proves absent in the same breath. tests/test_crew.py::test_double_dispatch_refuses_a_member_with_a_non_terminal_run and every test in tests/test_member_guard_counts_live_processes.py pass, and a new assertion fails if any of them would change verdict when the chosen pid's occupancy changes - state in the manifest how that assertion would catch a regression. Ruff check and format over exactly the staged paths add no findings beyond the same paths at the base revision, with both counts pasted into the manifest as digits.
